newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hyal suspended, in Canada dispute.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hyal suspended, in Canada dispute.

text.p: Hyal Pharmaceuticals Australia Ltd said on Tuesday it had requested that its stock be suspended from trade on the Australian Stock Exchange.
The company said it was considering a proposal for a significant change in activities in light of a dispute with the parent company, which is based in Canada.

"...We believe that the circumstances of the dispute give rise to a situation whereby the market is not fully informed and ask that HPA shares be suspended from trading," Hyal said in a statement accompanying the ASX notice.
The Hyal statement carried a topic line entitled "Proposal for significant change in activities in light of dispute with parent company."

"It is noted that the issue of suspension will be discussed in a meeting with Messrs O'Hara and Walsh (ASX officer based in Perth) later today and understand that in the meantime HPA shares will be suspended from trading," it said.
The Australian company (HPA) is 60 percent owned by Hyal Pharmaceutical Corp.

The Tuesday edition of The Australian newspaper said in an article by columnist Bryan Frith that it was believed the Canadian company would call a shareholders meeting to replace nearly all of the directors on the local board.

"HPA is unhappy that improvements which it has made remain the property of its parent," the paper said. "There are suggestions HPA has indicated it no longer wants to use Hyal technology but will go its own way." Hyal shares fell one cent to 39 cents on Monday. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
